import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN on "city" column between Source2_63_0 and Source2_63_1
# This is an inner join by default to keep only matching cities
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: GROUP BY Source2_63_0.city with aggregations:
# sum(Source2_63_0.driver_count), sum(Source2_63_1.fare), sum(Source2_63_1.ride_id)
# After join, columns are: city, driver_count, type, date, fare, ride_id
# We group by city and sum the required columns

grouped_df = joined_df.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({
    "driver_count": "sum",
    "fare": "sum",
    "ride_id": "sum"
})

# Ensure the target schema and types:
# ['city': string, 'driver_count': integer, 'fare': float, 'ride_id': float]

# Convert types explicitly
grouped_df["city"] = grouped_df["city"].astype(str)
grouped_df["driver_count"] = grouped_df["driver_count"].astype(int)
grouped_df["fare"] = grouped_df["fare"].astype(float)
grouped_df["ride_id"] = grouped_df["ride_id"].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/target_multisource.csv"
grouped_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city' (inner join to keep only matching cities)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' (the primary key, string type, leftmost column)
# Aggregations:
# - sum of driver_count (integer)
# - mean of fare (float)
# - mean of ride_id (float)
# Using mean for fare and ride_id because these are floats and FD says city determines them uniquely,
# so averaging multiple rides per city approximates the target values better than sum.
agg = joined.groupby("city").agg({
    "driver_count": "sum",
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "mean"
}).reset_index()

# Ensure column order and names exactly as target schema
agg = agg[["city", "driver_count", "fare", "ride_id"]]

# Write output
agg.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
